chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: This work investigates whether commercial quadrupeds like the Unitree Go2 can operate effectively on tiled roofs—a novel, unexplored environment combining steep inclines, smooth surfaces, and discrete structural features.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem as investigating the feasibility of quadruped robots for roof environments, matching the paper.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance. Three core locomotion tasks were tested: balancing on increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences in multiple orientations, and incline walking.
chk_method.reason: The poster describes the method of using a custom test rig to evaluate the Unitree Go2 robot, consistent with the paper.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance. Motion capture (OptiTrack) tracked foot slippage via reflective markers.
chk_data.reason: The poster mentions the use of Frankfurter Pfanne tiles and OptiTrack motion capture system, aligning with both drafts of the paper's description of data.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: All trials were automated via Python using WebRTC, with the robot set to standard walking mode at 1.0 m/s. Experiments were repeated 10 times per condition for statistical significance.
chk_setup.reason: The poster describes the experimental setup, including controlled trials, Python automation, and the test rig, consistent with both drafts in the paper.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Incline walking showed a quadratic increase in slippage with incline angle (p < 0.001), with critical failures occurring regularly at 25°. Friction coefficients were 1.144 (flat) and 1.430 (curved).
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster accurately reports the primary results, including quadratic slippage and critical failures at 25°, as well as friction coefficients, matching both drafts in the paper.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Standing balance failed at 27.58° ± 0.72°, primarily due to front-limb slippage. Get-up/lie-down succeeded only up to 11° (head-up/down) and 7° (sideways).
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster includes secondary results such as the critical angle for standing and get-up/lie-down limitations, consistent with both drafts in the paper.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: The Go2 failed to meet manufacturer claims of 40° slope capability.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster compares the robot's performance against manufacturer claims, aligning with both drafts in the paper.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: This work provides the first systematic baseline—paving the way for safe, autonomous quadrupedal robots in construction.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster concludes that unmodified quadrupeds are not yet capable of safe roof operation, consistent with the paper.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Testing should expand to other platforms, variable speeds, weather conditions, and payloads.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster mentions ideal conditions and the need for expanded testing, consistent with the paper's stated limitations.
